meta.name: Agent & GitHub CLI Catalog
meta.notes: Structured data layer behind apps/claude-code-catalog.html. The GitHub family is complete here; the Claude and Codex families cover the most-used surface, with the full 504-entry set still living in the embedded encyclopedia dataset. Add records here without touching rendering code.

entries.name: Native installer
entries.description: One-line installer that manages its own launcher and updates itself in the background.
entries.note: On native Windows install Git for Windows too, or the Bash tool is unavailable and Claude Code falls back to PowerShell.

entries.name: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
entries.description: Install through npm when you already manage Node tooling that way.

entries.name: claude update
entries.description: Check for and install a newer version immediately.

entries.name: autoUpdatesChannel
entries.description: Choose whether the client tracks the latest or the stable release channel.
entries.note: The channel you install from becomes the default; this key changes it afterwards.

entries.name: claude
entries.description: Start an interactive session in the current directory.

entries.name: claude -p "query"
entries.description: Run headlessly, print the result, and exit. The basis of every scripted use.
entries.note: Combine with --output-format json when a script needs to parse the result rather than display it.

entries.name: claude -c
entries.description: Continue the most recent conversation in this directory.

entries.name: claude -r
entries.description: Resume a specific past session, by id or by picking from a list.

entries.name: claude auth login
entries.description: Sign in to an Anthropic account, or add --console for a Console account.

entries.name: claude auth status
entries.description: Report the current authentication state as JSON.

entries.name: claude doctor
entries.description: Run installation, settings and connectivity diagnostics.
entries.note: Start here when the client launches but behaves oddly; it validates settings files that would otherwise fail silently.

entries.name: claude mcp
entries.description: Manage Model Context Protocol servers from the shell.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
examples.label: add

entries.name: claude config
entries.description: Read and write settings from the shell instead of editing JSON by hand.

entries.name: --model
entries.description: Choose the model for the session.

entries.name: --permission-mode
entries.description: Start in a specific permission mode.
entries.note: plan mode makes Claude propose an approach and wait for approval before touching anything.

entries.name: --output-format
entries.description: Select text, json or stream-json output in print mode.

entries.name: --allowedTools
entries.description: Pre-approve specific tools so a headless run does not stop for prompts.
entries.note: Scope Bash rules tightly; Bash(*) hands over the whole shell.

entries.name: --add-dir
entries.description: Give the session access to directories outside the current working directory.

entries.name: --append-system-prompt
entries.description: Append extra standing instructions for one session.

entries.name: --verbose
entries.description: Show full turn-by-turn output instead of the condensed view.

entries.name: /clear
entries.description: Discard the current conversation context and start fresh in the same session.
entries.note: Cheaper and more predictable than letting a long context auto-compact when you are switching tasks.

entries.name: /compact
entries.description: Summarise the conversation so far to reclaim context window.

entries.name: /model
entries.description: Switch models mid-session.

entries.name: /config
entries.description: Open the settings editor, including theme, editor mode and notifications.

entries.name: /review
entries.description: Review a pull request or the working diff from inside a session.

entries.name: /init
entries.description: Generate a CLAUDE.md that documents the current codebase.

entries.name: /agents
entries.description: Create, edit and inspect the subagents available to this project.

entries.name: /mcp
entries.description: Inspect MCP server status and authenticate servers that need OAuth.

entries.name: /resume
entries.description: Pick an earlier session to continue.

entries.name: /help
entries.description: List the slash commands available in this session, including project ones.

entries.name: settings.json scopes
entries.description: Three files merge into the effective configuration, most specific winning.
entries.note: Put anything machine-specific or secret in settings.local.json, which is gitignored by default.

entries.name: permissions
entries.description: Allow, ask and deny lists that gate tool use before the model ever runs.
entries.note: deny wins over allow. Denying Read on secret files is worth doing even in a trusted repo.

entries.name: env
entries.description: Environment variables injected into every session and tool call.
entries.note: Do not put credentials here if the file is committed; use settings.local.json.

entries.name: model
entries.description: Default model for sessions started in this scope.

entries.name: hooks
entries.description: Commands to run at lifecycle events, keyed by event and tool matcher.

entries.name: statusLine
entries.description: Command whose output renders as the session status line.

entries.name: Rule syntax
entries.description: A rule is Tool or Tool(specifier); the specifier is matched by the client, not the model.
entries.note: The :* suffix is a prefix match, not a shell glob. Bash(npm test:*) allows any command starting with npm test.

entries.name: Permission modes
entries.description: How much the session may do before asking.

examples.label: ask on first use of each tool

entries.note: bypassPermissions removes the last guardrail; reserve it for throwaway containers.

entries.name: /permissions
entries.description: Review and edit the active rules from inside a session.

entries.name: PreToolUse
entries.description: Runs before a tool call. A non-zero exit blocks the call.
entries.note: The only hook that can veto an action; the rest observe or react.

entries.name: PostToolUse
entries.description: Runs after a tool call succeeds. The usual place for formatters and linters.

entries.name: SessionStart
entries.description: Runs when a session begins. Used to install dependencies or warm a dev server.

entries.name: UserPromptSubmit
entries.description: Runs when a prompt is submitted; can inject extra context or reject the prompt.

entries.name: Stop
entries.description: Runs when the assistant finishes a turn. Useful for notifications.

entries.name: claude mcp add
entries.description: Register an MCP server over stdio, HTTP or SSE.

examples.command: claude mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
examples.label: http

entries.name: claude mcp list
entries.description: List configured servers and whether each one is connected.

entries.name: MCP scopes
entries.description: Where a server registration lives: local to you, shared with the project, or user-wide.
entries.note: project scope writes .mcp.json, which teammates get on checkout — so never put a token in the command.

entries.name: MCP tool naming
entries.description: MCP tools appear as mcp__server__tool in permission rules and hook matchers.

entries.name: Subagents
entries.description: Markdown files defining a delegated agent with its own prompt, model and tool access.
entries.note: A subagent starts with no memory of the current conversation, so its prompt has to be self-contained.

entries.name: Skills
entries.description: Packaged instructions that load on demand when a task matches their description.

entries.name: Custom slash commands
entries.description: Markdown files in a commands directory become slash commands.

entries.name: Plugins
entries.description: Distributable bundles of commands, agents, skills, hooks and MCP servers.

entries.name: CLAUDE.md
entries.description: Standing project instructions, read at the start of every session in that directory.
entries.note: Nested files are additive: a subdirectory's CLAUDE.md layers on top of the root one rather than replacing it.

entries.name: @ imports
entries.description: Pull another file into CLAUDE.md instead of duplicating its content.

entries.name: # quick memory
entries.description: Start a message with # to append a note to memory without opening the file.

examples.command: # always run the linter before committing
examples.label: session

entries.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
entries.description: API key used when authenticating against the Anthropic API rather than a subscription login.
entries.note: Not needed for a normal Claude or Console account login; setting it changes which billing path is used.

entries.name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK
entries.description: Route requests through Amazon Bedrock instead of the Anthropic API.

entries.name: MAX_THINKING_TOKENS
entries.description: Raise the budget available for extended thinking.

entries.name: DISABLE_TELEMETRY
entries.description: Opt out of usage telemetry and error reporting.

entries.name: codex
entries.description: Start OpenAI's terminal agent interactively.

entries.name: codex exec
entries.description: Run non-interactively and print the result — the Codex analogue of claude -p.

entries.name: codex resume
entries.description: Continue a previous Codex session.

entries.name: codex --sandbox
entries.description: Choose how much filesystem and network access the agent gets.
entries.note: workspace-write confines writes to the working directory; network access stays off unless it is enabled separately.

entries.name: codex mcp
entries.description: Manage MCP servers for Codex.

examples.command: codex mcp add my-server -- npx -y my-mcp-server
examples.label: add

entries.name: config.toml
entries.description: Codex configuration file, holding model, sandbox and provider settings.

entries.name: AGENTS.md
entries.description: Standing instructions for Codex, the counterpart to CLAUDE.md.
entries.note: The AGENTS.md convention is shared across several agent tools, so one file can serve more than one of them.

entries.name: approval_policy
entries.description: When Codex pauses to ask before acting.

examples.label: ask only after a command fails

entries.name: gh auth login
entries.description: Authenticate with a GitHub host. Interactive by default; reads a token from stdin with --with-token for CI.
entries.note: A token supplied through the GH_TOKEN environment variable is used automatically and takes precedence over a stored login.

entries.name: gh auth status
entries.description: Show which account is active on each host, the token source, and the scopes it carries.
entries.note: The first thing to run when a gh command returns 403 — a missing scope looks identical to a permissions problem.

entries.name: gh auth token
entries.description: Print the stored token for a host on stdout so other tools can consume it.
entries.note: Never echo this into a log or a committed file; treat the output the same as a password.

entries.name: gh auth refresh
entries.description: Add scopes to the existing credential without a full re-login.

entries.name: gh auth setup-git
entries.description: Register gh as a git credential helper so plain git push and git clone reuse the gh login.

entries.name: gh auth switch
entries.description: Change the active account when several are signed in to the same host.

entries.name: gh auth logout
entries.description: Remove stored credentials for a host.

entries.name: gh repo create
entries.description: Create a repository, either empty on GitHub or from the current directory.
entries.note: --source=. reuses the current git repo and adds the remote; without it gh creates an empty repository instead.

entries.name: gh repo clone
entries.description: Clone a repository using the gh credential, accepting OWNER/REPO shorthand.
entries.note: Arguments after -- are passed straight through to git clone.

entries.name: gh repo fork
entries.description: Fork a repository and optionally clone it, wiring up an upstream remote.

entries.name: gh repo view
entries.description: Print a repository's README and metadata, or open it in a browser.

entries.name: gh repo list
entries.description: List repositories owned by a user or organization.

entries.name: gh repo sync
entries.description: Bring a fork up to date with its upstream, locally or on GitHub.
entries.note: Refuses to run when the histories have diverged unless you pass --force, which discards local commits.

entries.name: gh repo set-default
entries.description: Choose which repository gh targets in a clone that has several remotes.
entries.note: Set this in a fork, or gh pr create may open the pull request against the wrong repository.

entries.name: gh repo edit
entries.description: Change description, homepage, topics, visibility or enabled features.

entries.name: gh repo rename
entries.description: Rename a repository and update the local remote to match.
entries.note: GitHub redirects the old URL, but CI configs and badges that hardcode the name still need updating.

entries.name: gh repo archive
entries.description: Mark a repository read-only without deleting it.

entries.name: gh repo delete
entries.description: Permanently delete a repository.
entries.note: Irreversible. Needs the delete_repo scope, which gh auth refresh --scopes delete_repo can add.

entries.name: gh repo deploy-key
entries.description: List, add or remove deploy keys for a repository.

entries.name: gh pr create
entries.description: Open a pull request from the current branch.

examples.command: gh pr create --base main --head feature --reviewer octocat --label enhancement
examples.label: targeted

entries.note: --fill reuses the commit subject and body, which is why a good commit message pays off twice.

entries.name: gh pr list
entries.description: List pull requests with filters, or as JSON for scripting.

entries.name: gh pr view
entries.description: Show a pull request's description, metadata and optionally its comments.
entries.note: With no number, gh uses the pull request associated with the current branch.

entries.name: gh pr checkout
entries.description: Check out a pull request's branch locally, including from a fork.

entries.name: gh pr diff
entries.description: Show the diff a pull request would apply.

entries.name: gh pr checks
entries.description: Show CI check results for a pull request, and optionally block until they finish.
entries.note: --watch exits non-zero when a required check fails, which makes it usable as a gate in a script.

entries.name: gh pr review
entries.description: Submit a review: approve, request changes, or leave a comment.

examples.command: gh pr review 42 --request-changes --body 'Needs a test for the empty case'
examples.label: changes

entries.note: GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request; the command fails rather than silently doing nothing.

entries.name: gh pr merge
entries.description: Merge a pull request with the strategy the repository allows.
entries.note: --auto queues the merge for when checks pass instead of failing immediately; --admin bypasses branch protection and should be rare.

entries.name: gh pr ready
entries.description: Flip a draft pull request to ready for review, or back to draft.

entries.name: gh pr comment
entries.description: Add a comment to a pull request thread.

entries.name: gh pr edit
entries.description: Change a pull request's metadata after it is open.

entries.name: gh pr close
entries.description: Close a pull request without merging it.

entries.name: gh pr reopen
entries.description: Reopen a closed pull request.

entries.name: gh pr status
entries.description: Summarise the pull requests that involve you: yours, assigned, and awaiting your review.

entries.name: gh issue create
entries.description: File a new issue.

examples.command: gh issue create --title 'Dark mode contrast on cards' --body-file report.md
examples.label: shell

entries.name: gh issue list
entries.description: List issues with filters, or as JSON.

entries.name: gh issue view
entries.description: Read an issue and its discussion.

entries.name: gh issue comment
entries.description: Add a comment to an issue.

entries.name: gh issue edit
entries.description: Change an issue's labels, assignees, milestone, title or body.

entries.name: gh issue close
entries.description: Close an issue, optionally recording why.

examples.command: gh issue close 17 --reason 'not planned' --comment 'Out of scope'
examples.label: shell

entries.name: gh issue reopen
entries.description: Reopen a closed issue.

entries.name: gh issue develop
entries.description: Create a branch linked to an issue so the pull request closes it automatically.

entries.name: gh issue transfer
entries.description: Move an issue to another repository.

entries.name: gh issue pin
entries.description: Pin an issue to the top of the repository's issue list.
entries.note: A repository can have at most three pinned issues.

entries.name: gh issue status
entries.description: Show the issues assigned to you, opened by you, or mentioning you.

entries.name: gh workflow list
entries.description: List the workflows defined in a repository.

entries.name: gh workflow view
entries.description: Show a workflow's recent runs, or print its YAML.

entries.name: gh workflow run
entries.description: Trigger a workflow_dispatch run, passing any declared inputs.

examples.command: gh workflow run deploy.yml -f environment=staging -f dry_run=true
examples.label: with inputs

entries.note: Only works if the workflow declares a workflow_dispatch trigger, and only on a ref where that file already exists.

entries.name: gh workflow enable
entries.description: Re-enable a workflow that was disabled manually or by inactivity.
entries.note: GitHub disables scheduled workflows in public repositories after 60 days without activity.

entries.name: gh run list
entries.description: List recent workflow runs, filtered by workflow, branch or status.

entries.name: gh run view
entries.description: Inspect one run, including step results and logs.
entries.note: --log-failed is the fastest path to a CI failure; it skips the passing steps entirely.

entries.name: gh run watch
entries.description: Follow a run live and exit when it finishes.
entries.note: --exit-status makes the command return non-zero on failure, so it can gate a deploy script.

entries.name: gh run rerun
entries.description: Re-run a workflow run, all of it or just what failed.
entries.note: Re-running is for a confirmed infrastructure flake. A test that fails twice is a real failure, not a flake.

entries.name: gh run cancel
entries.description: Stop a run that is still in progress.

entries.name: gh run download
entries.description: Download the artifacts a run produced.

entries.name: gh cache list
entries.description: List and prune the Actions caches a repository is holding.
entries.note: Caches count against a repository storage limit, and a stale cache is a common cause of a green local build going red in CI.

entries.name: gh secret set
entries.description: Store an encrypted secret for Actions, an environment, or an organization.

examples.command: gh secret set NPM_TOKEN --org my-org --visibility selected --repos web,api
examples.label: org

entries.note: Prefer the interactive prompt or --body-file over --body, which puts the secret into your shell history.

entries.name: gh secret list
entries.description: List secret names and when they were last updated. Values are never readable.

entries.name: gh variable set
entries.description: Store a non-secret configuration value that workflows read through vars.

entries.name: gh release create
entries.description: Create a tagged release and attach build artifacts to it.
entries.note: --generate-notes builds the changelog from merged pull request titles, which rewards descriptive PR titles.

entries.name: gh release list
entries.description: List a repository's releases.

entries.name: gh release view
entries.description: Show a release's notes and asset list.
entries.note: With no tag, gh shows the latest release.

entries.name: gh release download
entries.description: Download assets from a release.

entries.name: gh release upload
entries.description: Attach more files to an existing release.

entries.name: gh release edit
entries.description: Change a release's notes, tag, or draft and prerelease flags.

entries.name: gh release delete
entries.description: Delete a release, optionally removing its git tag too.

entries.name: gh gist create
entries.description: Publish files as a gist.

examples.command: cat results.json | gh gist create --filename results.json
examples.label: from stdin

entries.note: Gists default to secret, which means unlisted rather than private — anyone with the URL can read one.

entries.name: gh gist list
entries.description: List, view, edit or clone your gists.

entries.name: gh api
entries.description: Call any REST endpoint with authentication and pagination handled for you.

examples.command: gh api -X PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo} -f description='New description'
examples.label: write

entries.note: {owner} and {repo} are substituted from the current repository. Use -f for string fields and -F to read a value from a file or interpret it as a number or boolean.

entries.name: gh api graphql
entries.description: Run a GraphQL query, which is the only way to reach some data such as Projects v2.

examples.command: gh api graphql -f query='{ viewer { login } }'
examples.label: query

examples.command: gh api graphql --paginate -F owner=cli -F name=cli -f query=@query.graphql
examples.label: from file

entries.name: --json / --jq / --template
entries.description: The scripting triad shared by most gh commands: select fields, filter them, then format.
entries.note: Run a command with --json and no field list to print every field that command supports.

entries.name: gh search
entries.description: Search repositories, issues, pull requests, code or commits across GitHub.

entries.name: gh browse
entries.description: Open the current repository, a file, or a line range in a browser.
entries.note: Add --no-browser to print the URL instead of opening it, which makes it a permalink generator.

entries.name: gh status
entries.description: Show your notifications, review requests and mentions across repositories.

entries.name: gh extension install
entries.description: Install, list, upgrade or author gh extensions.
entries.note: An extension is any executable named gh-something on your PATH, so a shell script is enough to make one.

entries.name: gh alias set
entries.description: Save a long gh invocation under a short name.

examples.command: gh alias set bugs 'issue list --label bug --state open'
examples.label: shell

examples.command: gh alias set --shell review 'gh pr checkout $1 && gh pr diff'
examples.label: shell alias

entries.name: gh label
entries.description: Manage a repository's labels, including copying a set between repositories.

examples.command: gh label create needs-repro --color FBCA04 --description 'Cannot reproduce yet'
examples.label: create

entries.name: gh project
entries.description: Work with Projects v2 boards: list projects, add items, and read fields.
entries.note: Needs the project scope; add it with gh auth refresh --scopes read:project,project.

entries.name: gh codespace
entries.description: Create, list, connect to and stop codespaces.

entries.name: gh ruleset
entries.description: Inspect the rulesets that protect branches and tags, and see which ones apply to a branch.
entries.note: gh ruleset check explains why a push was rejected far faster than reading settings in the browser.

entries.name: gh attestation verify
entries.description: Verify the build provenance attestation attached to an artifact.

entries.name: gh config set
entries.description: Persist a gh preference such as editor, pager or git protocol.

entries.name: GH_TOKEN
entries.description: The token gh authenticates with, overriding any stored login. GITHUB_TOKEN is accepted as a fallback.
entries.note: Inside GitHub Actions the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN is scoped to that repository and expires when the job ends.

entries.name: GH_HOST
entries.description: Target a GitHub Enterprise Server host when the current directory gives no clue.

entries.name: GH_REPO
entries.description: Run a command against a repository without being inside its clone.

entries.name: GH_FORCE_TTY
entries.description: Force the rich terminal rendering when gh output is piped or captured.
entries.note: Without this gh strips colour and layout as soon as stdout is not a terminal.

entries.name: GH_CONFIG_DIR
entries.description: Where gh keeps config.yml and hosts.yml, and how to relocate them.
entries.note: hosts.yml holds the OAuth tokens; back it up like a credential file, not like a config file.

entries.name: gh --version
entries.description: Print the installed gh version and check whether a newer one exists.

entries.name: git push -u origin <branch>
entries.description: Push a new branch and set its upstream so later pushes and pulls need no arguments.
entries.note: The -u only matters on the first push; afterwards plain git push is enough.

entries.name: git fetch origin pull/ID/head
entries.description: Fetch a pull request's head commit directly, without the gh CLI.

examples.command: git fetch origin pull/42/head:pr-42 && git switch pr-42
examples.label: shell

entries.note: Useful on a machine with no gh installed; gh pr checkout does the same thing and also configures the push remote.

entries.name: git diff base...HEAD
entries.description: Show what a pull request actually changes, using the three-dot form.
entries.note: Three dots compare against the merge base, so unrelated commits landing on main do not pollute the diff. Two dots do not.

entries.name: git switch -c
entries.description: Create and check out a branch. The modern replacement for git checkout -b.

entries.name: git worktree add
entries.description: Check out a second branch into its own directory, without stashing the current one.
entries.note: Far safer than stashing when you need to look at another branch mid-task; both checkouts stay live.

entries.name: git rebase origin/main
entries.description: Replay your commits on top of the latest base branch.

examples.command: git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
examples.label: update a branch

entries.note: Rewrites commit hashes, so never rebase a branch someone else has checked out. Merge instead on shared branches.

entries.name: git merge origin/main
entries.description: Bring the base branch into your pull request branch, keeping everyone's checkout valid.

examples.command: git fetch origin && git merge origin/main
examples.label: resolve a conflict

entries.note: Preferred over rebase when the branch is already pushed and under review.

entries.name: git restore
entries.description: Discard working-tree changes or unstage a file, without the overloaded checkout verb.
entries.note: git restore without --staged throws away uncommitted work irreversibly. Check git status first.

entries.name: git stash -u
entries.description: Set aside work in progress, including untracked files.
entries.note: Plain git stash leaves untracked files behind, which is how new files get lost during a branch switch.

entries.name: git cherry-pick
entries.description: Copy one commit onto the current branch, for backports and hotfixes.

entries.name: git blame -L
entries.description: Find which commit last touched a specific range of lines.
entries.note: git log -S searches for when a string was added or removed, which usually beats blame for finding the origin of a behaviour.

entries.name: .github/ conventions
entries.description: The files GitHub reads from a repository to shape its interface and automation.
entries.note: CODEOWNERS is read from .github/, the repository root, or docs/ — the first match wins.
